result.title: Deep LLM layers expose passage-level context in EEG during silent reading
result.comment: 41 pages (including 23 pages of Supplementary Material), 12 figures (including 5 in Supplementary Material)
result.summary: In a previous report we showed that a decoder can recover open-vocabulary word-level information from 19-channel EEG recorded during silent reading, by aligning short EEG windows with hidden-state embeddings of the presented word taken from a large language model (LLM). That analysis contrasted two of the model's 33 layers: the context-free input embedding and one mid-depth layer. Here we ask how EEG-decodable structure is distributed over the full depth of the language model. We trained one decoder per layer of Llama-3.1-8B, with and without a causal transformer over the sequence of EEG windows. We distinguish word-level decodability from a context-tracking component. Word-level decodability peaks in early layers and declines steadily towards the last layer. In contrast, the context-tracking component of the retrieval gain rises with depth, both with and without a causal transformer. Unexpectedly, a decoder that sees a single 0.5-s window at a time tracks the text passage too. Two new controls dissect this component. A target-geometry control, a synthetic predictor made of the true target plus noise calibrated to each decoder's word-level accuracy, shows that context tracking is not a by-product of word decoding and target geometry. A control that permutes predictions across runs from either the same or from different sessions shows that most of the observed context-tracking is not caused by an EEG recording session signature. Instead, context tracking mostly follows the text. A single EEG window therefore carries passage-level information that a contextual target can absorb. The results locate word identity in the early layers of the language model, discourse state in the deeper layers, and make the choice of target layer a design dial for EEG language decoders.

AI.brief_summary: 该研究为 Llama-3.1-8B 的每一层分别训练 EEG 解码器，把默读时的 0.5 秒脑电窗口对齐到各层隐状态，比较词级可解码性与上下文追踪成分随模型深度的变化。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「逐层探测 + 分离局部词身份与上下文追踪成分 + 目标几何对照」的分析框架可供核查，或能借鉴用于判断 LVR 内部状态中细节与语境信息分别落在哪个深度、以及目标层选择作为设计旋钮；与主线仅为方法层面的潜在联系。
